subject: Turn-up handshake: GPU pool provisioning & autoscale plan
messages:
From: irene_choi@redwood.ai
To: sarah.jenkins@peregrinetx.com, dan.simpson@peregrinetx.com
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 14 Jul 2027 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Turn-up handshake: GPU pool provisioning & autoscale plan

Hi Sarah / Dan —

Thanks again for choosing Redwood for your inference layer. To make the dedicated pool turn-up smooth, I wanted to align on a short activation playbook and a few decisions we need from your side before we schedule the canary. Proposed agenda for this thread / meeting: 

- Confirm regional placement and data residency constraints
- Agree min/max pool sizing and burst policy for peak traffic
- Canary / traffic-shift approach and rollback gates
- Network & NetOps prerequisites (vPC peering, IP allowlist)
- Timeline and procurement sign-off items (deal id below)

Attachments: turnup-runbook.pdf (activation steps), regional-capacity-map.csv (proposed nodes by region).

Quick asks for your reply: please confirm (1) preferred region for initial turn-up (us-west-2 vs eu-west-1), (2) target steady-state RPS and peak bursts, and (3) three 2-hour windows next week you can run a canary.

I'll loop Monica (implementation lead) and Ben (solutions engineer) for runbook details. Rishi is on copy for procurement questions.

Thanks —
Irene Choi
Head of Implementation Programs
Redwood Inference

From: sarah.jenkins@peregrinetx.com
To: irene_choi@redwood.ai
Cc: dan.simpson@peregrinetx.com, monica_patel@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 14 Jul 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Turn-up handshake: GPU pool provisioning & autoscale plan

Irene — thanks, this is helpful. A few quick constraints from our side:

- Region: prefer eu-west-1 for the initial pilot (data residency & compliance). We can expand to us-west-2 later.
- Traffic: steady-state expected ~45 RPS inference traffic (token-generation workloads), peaks up to ~450 RPS during batch reprocess windows.
- SLOs: we require 99th percentile <= 220ms for interactive calls; background batch jobs can tolerate higher latency.
- Security: will need SOC2 evidence and confirmation that KV cache is isolated per-customer.

Availability for a canary: next Tue 7/20 09:00-11:00 CEST or Wed 7/21 14:00-16:00 CEST.

Also: can you confirm expected billable units for burst traffic so our finance team can budget?

—Sarah
Sarah Jenkins
VP Engineering, Peregrine Therapeutics

From: monica_patel@redwood.ai
To: sarah.jenkins@peregrinetx.com, dan.simpson@peregrinetx.com
Cc: irene_choi@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 15 Jul 2027 09:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Turn-up handshake: GPU pool provisioning & autoscale plan

Hi Sarah / Dan —

Thanks for the quick reply and the numbers; that helps a lot. Attached is a first-draft activation plan and runbook (turnup-runbook.pdf) and a compact regional-capacity spreadsheet (regional-capacity-map.csv). Summary below: 

1) Proposed initial topology (eu-west-1 pilot)
- Dedicated pool: 6 T4s (min), scaled to 30 T4s (max) for bursts
- Warm VMs prepped with quantized r/w model variant to reduce cold-starts
- KV cache: customer-isolated per pool, nightly TTL of 48h (configurable)

2) Autoscale & burst policy
- Scale triggers: avg queue latency > 80ms OR 95th token latency > 150ms
- Min nodes: 6 (guarantees capacity for steady-state 45 RPS)
- Max nodes during burst: 30 (handles short 10x traffic spikes)
- Burst window: allowed 4x sustained bursts per 24h; overage >4 triggers ops alert and optional temporary capacity extension (billing as burst units)

3) Canary plan (recommended)
- Step 0: Network prep & IP allowlist validation (NetOps)
- Step 1: Deploy pool to eu-west-1 staging, dry-run with synthetic traffic
- Step 2: 2-hour canary with 10% production traffic ramp to 100% of steady-state, monitor 99p latency and error rate
- Rollback gate: 99p latency >250ms OR error increase >1.5x baseline -> immediate roll back to hosted model route

4) Ops & handoff
- On-call rotation: Redwood SRE on-call for turn-up window (Ben lead)
- Post-canary 48h stabilization before full cutover

Open items for you to confirm: EU region ok? Accept min/max node counts above? Approve burst policy thresholds? If yes, we'll schedule the canary for Tue 7/20 09:00 CEST as proposed.

Attachments: turnup-runbook.pdf, regional-capacity-map.csv

Regards,
Monica Patel
Implementation Lead, Customer Success
Redwood Inference

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: monica_patel@redwood.ai, irene_choi@redwood.ai, sarah.jenkins@peregrinetx.com
Cc: dan.simpson@peregrinetx.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 15 Jul 2027 11:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Turn-up handshake: GPU pool provisioning & autoscale plan

Following Monica's plan — engineering notes / clarifications:

- Kernel & model variant: for eu-west-1 pilot we'll use the quantized int8 variant (QKV-friendly kernels) to reduce mem pressure; this gives ~1.8x throughput vs fp16 in our tests for these model families.
- Warm-up strategy: pre-warm KV cache with the top 25 most common prefixes (we can provide a list if Peregrine shares sample prompts) and keep one warm worker per node for fast path.
- Autoscale warm window: when a scale-up is triggered, nodes are added in rolling batches of 3 with a 30s stagger to avoid thundering; expected scale latency ~60-90s to effective capacity.
- Metrics we'll stream to your monitoring: token-per-second, 95p/99p latency, GPU util, evictions per-minute, and queue depth.

Attached ops-checklist.md with exact runbook commands and telemetry endpoints. One ask for Dan: please confirm whether your SRE team can accept Prometheus pushes or if we should open a read-only project in your monitoring account.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: dan.simpson@peregrinetx.com
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai, irene_choi@redwood.ai
Cc: sarah.jenkins@peregrinetx.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 16 Jul 2027 08:55:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Turn-up handshake: GPU pool provisioning & autoscale plan

Ben / Monica — thanks for the detail. A couple of follow-ups inline: 

> pre-warm KV cache with the top 25 most common prefixes
Can you outline the mechanism? Will Redwood accept a static list we upload, or do you have an ingestion endpoint? Also: we run a daily batch at 02:00 CET that floods the system for ~30 minutes — would that count as one of the 4 allowed bursts per 24h?

> metrics we'll stream to your monitoring
We prefer a read-only Prometheus scrape from a Redwood exporter; our security team will not accept push endpoints. Please provide the exporter endpoint and the scrape interval you recommend.

Canary schedule: Tue 7/20 09:00 CEST works for us. Please send calendar invite and the sign-off checklist.

—Dan
Dan Simpson
SRE Lead, Peregrine Therapeutics

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai

Sarah / Dan — wrapping up commercial and next-step items so everyone has a single source of truth: 

- Deal ID: DEAL-PTX-2027-07 (signed SOW received 2027-07-13).
- Billing: steady-state 6-node reserved monthly commit + burst units billed per-token during autoscale events; estimate for planned initial usage (45 RPS steady / occasional 450 RPS bursts): ~$24k/month (est). Final invoice depends on actual burst consumption.
- Procurement ask: We need a PO referencing DEAL-PTX-2027-07 before production cutover.
- Next meeting: Kickoff + canary coordination (Monica to share runbook and Ben to lead SRE ops) — calendar invite for Tue 2027-07-20 09:00 CEST will be sent by Monica.

Action items assigned:
- Monica: final runbook + calendar invite (by 7/18 EOD)
- Ben: exporter endpoint & ops checklist (provide by 7/19)
- Dan: confirm Prometheus scrape window & provide sample prefixes for KV pre-warm (by 7/19)
- Sarah / Procurement: PO prep (as soon as scheduling confirmed)

If there are no blockers, we plan the canary for Tue 7/20 09:00 CEST. Thanks all — looking forward to the turn-up.

Rishi Malhotra
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
